com: And it was written by Fahil ibn Muhammad ibn Fahil al-Saghir in Riyadh, 1424 AH, under the number 41961 at address 11531.
رضي: May Allāh be pleased with him/her/them.
التَّحَلِّي: The act of putting on or adorning with ornaments or decorations.
أن: Indeed, if a person were to perform an obligatory act within it, it would be as if he had performed seventy obligatory acts at other times.
رحمهُ: May Allah have mercy upon him.
اختَلَّ: اختَلَّ is translated as 'has become distorted' or 'has deviated'. However, considering the context of classical Islamic texts and maintaining brevity, it can be rendered as 'has gone astray'.
وَذَرِيعَةٌ: And a just and fair argument or reasoning.
تَقَرُّباً: as an act of seeking closeness (to Allah)
فَضَعِيْفٌ: وَضَعَ فَصْلًا قَالَ : أَمَا سَمَعتُمْ يَقُولُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرٍو وَأَمَا سَمَعتُمْ يَقُولُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ
الْمُعَنْعَنُ:: The one who is afflicted with trials
اطُّلِعَ: It has been revealed or made known.
مُخَالِفٍ: A person who opposes or goes against.
التَّعَمُّدُ: The act of deliberating or intending
احْتَجَرَ: He/She/They took a vow of silence or seclusion.
مُلاَبِسَاتٍ: clothes that are worn or used
وَسَلَّمُوا: And they sent greetings of peace (salutations)
السِّمَاعُ: The act of listening or hearing
أُجِيْزَ: A journey or a specific event is permitted.
مُنَاوَلَةً،: In a manner of handling or dealing with,
الطَّعْنُ: The act of attacking or criticizing
فَالتَّرْجِيْحُ: So then, the preponderance of evidence
السَّكَنِ: The سكن (Sukun) is a diacritical mark indicating no vowel sound follows the consonant.
أَلَّفَ: A group of people or animals
مُرَتَّبَانِ: مُرَتَّبَانِ is translated as 'well-arranged' or 'methodically organized'.
خَلْفَ: خلف (khalf) is an Arabic term that can be translated into English as 'behind', 'backside', or 'rear'. However, in a classical Islamic context, it often refers to the posterior part of something or someone.
جُمْلَةٍ: A sentence or a complete thought.
